stance_taxonomy.recognition: treats PA / alienating behaviours as a real, assessable phenomenon; operates or endorses PA-specific identification / mediation / reunification work in NZ
stance_taxonomy.critique: argues PA construct is operationalised against family-violence survivors in NZ Family Court; advocates DV/trauma-informed alternatives and tighter regulation of s.133 / s.46G report writers
stance_taxonomy.middle: engages both alienating-behaviour and family-violence frames; differential-diagnosis approach aligned with NZ Family Court Specialist Report Writer Practice Note and the post-2019 Te Korowai Ture-a-Whānau child-centred + safety-primary line

nz_context_notes: NZ Psychologists Board / Te Poari Kaimātai Hinengaro o Aotearoa is the statutory regulator under HPCAA 2003 with public register at https://register.psychologistsboard.org.nz/
Counsellors are not under HPCAA — self-regulated via NZAC; psychotherapists regulated by PBANZ with APANZ as the professional body; social workers regulated by SWRB

Care of Children Act 2004 s.133 governs specialist psychological reports on a child; Practice Note (2018) jointly settled by Principal Family Court Judge, MOJ, NZLS Family Law Section, NZPB, NZ Psychological Society and NZCCP
s.46G Care of Children Act 2004 governs counselling after proceedings commenced — the section under which alienation-aware therapy is most commonly court-ordered
No NZ appellate-level Re Y [2026] EWFC 38 equivalent restricting unregulated PA experts

Most active NZ recognition-camp practice: The Family Matters Centre (Jill Goldson, Auckland); Goldson Model adopted by NZ government for child-inclusive mediation in 'Bridging the Gap' online programme
Cross-jurisdictional ANZ peak body: PAANZ (Parental Alienation Australia and New Zealand), founded 2012, primarily Australia-based (Korosi Melbourne, Moriarty AU)

Most institutionally-weighted critique-camp voice: NZ Family Violence Death Review Committee (FVDRC) - chaired by Julia Tolmie 2011-2016 (lawyers entry 7); historical / continuing members include Denise Wilson (AUT) and Pauline Gulliver (Auckland)
